title: A healthy snack under ₹20
body: College students want a healthy snack under ₹20. Most millet and protein snacks cost ₹50 or more, so students buy fried chips instead.

title: Breakfast on the go
body: Office workers want a cheap, healthy breakfast they can eat on the go. Most skip breakfast or buy biscuits and tea at the station.

title: Summer without sunburn
body: Two-wheeler riders spend hours in the sun but sunscreen tubes cost ₹300 or more, so almost none of them use it.

title: Clean water taste
body: Families in towns with hard water dislike the taste of tap water but cannot afford a purifier.

title: Energy for the night shift
body: Delivery riders and night-shift workers want an energy drink that is cheaper and less sugary than the big brands.

title: Kitchen grease
body: Small dhabas and home kitchens struggle to clean oil and grease off steel vessels with soap bars.

title: Hair fall in hostels
body: Students living in hostels blame hard water for hair fall and want a cheap, gentle shampoo.

title: Kids' tiffin
body: Parents want a packaged tiffin snack children will actually eat that is not fried or full of sugar.

title: Monsoon smell
body: Clothes dried indoors during the monsoon smell damp, and families have no cheap fix.

title: Gym on a budget
body: Young people starting at the gym want protein but cannot afford ₹2,000 tubs of powder.

title: Mosquitoes at the shop
body: Small shopkeepers sit at open counters in the evening and want a cheap, safe way to keep mosquitoes off.

title: Tea-time without guilt
body: Older adults with diabetes want a tea-time snack that does not spike their sugar.
